comparator.name: African Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The live Leiden Study Guide product identifies a current 180-EC African Studies bachelor with three 60-EC years. The curriculum combines African history, literature and arts, linguistics, research methodology, international networks, climate and health, digital humanities, sustained Swahili study, a compulsory 25-EC Study in Africa period, practice-oriented research and a 10-EC African Studies thesis. Year 3 preserves 30 EC of genuine elective space. The programme description discusses three possible academic tracks, but the current curriculum product and programme-specific regulations do not establish a formal route that must be named for the normalized generic target, so route remains null. Anthropological Linguistics is selected from the current 5-EC bound-elective group under the official-order neutral tie-break. The current product lists two distinct 10-EC modules named Swahili II in different years (codes 5731V015Y and 5733V005Y); both official curriculum entries are preserved separately rather than silently corrected. The zero-credit Thesis Seminar is noted here but omitted from the positive-credit component list.

exception.reason: Leiden African Studies is defined by sustained area-specific study: African history, literature, arts, languages, international networks, diaspora, climate and health; cumulative Swahili study; Africa-focused methodology; a compulsory 25-EC study period in Africa; practice-oriented research; and an African Studies thesis. UCR has a strong interdisciplinary humanities and social-science catalogue and one course devoted specifically to African art and heritage, but it does not offer an African Studies, African history, African politics, African literature, African linguistics or African-language sequence, an Africa-based field-study component or an African Studies research environment. Filling 24 UCR places mainly with general history, sociology, politics, media, literature and heritage would replace the programme's defining regional knowledge, language acquisition and situated research with adjacent disciplines. No defensible closest 24-course UCR programme can therefore be formed.
exception.curriculumContext: The live 2026-2027 Leiden curriculum product accounts for exactly 180 EC across three 60-EC years. It identifies 60 EC of compulsory first-year African Studies, language and methods work; 60 EC of second-year digital humanities, Africa-specific thematic study, language, research and the 25-EC Study in Africa; and a third year comprising 15 EC of compulsory Africa Today and Swahili III, 30 EC of genuine elective space, one 5-EC bound elective and the 10-EC African Studies thesis. Anthropological Linguistics is selected from the two current bound electives by official order. The duplicate Swahili II titles attached to distinct official module codes are retained transparently.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx (SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879), including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage provides the only course centered specifically on Africa and supports art, representation, heritage and decolonial questions. GOSHIST111 Modern History and GOSHIST211 History of Empires contribute broad historical frameworks; GOSPOLI112 Foundations of Comparative Politics, GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations, GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology, GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology and GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology provide transferable social-scientific concepts and methods; MCCMEDI311 Media & Race, MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature and MCCHEAM312 Modern Art & Modern Museums support representation, diaspora-adjacent, literary and heritage questions. These courses do not create sustained African history, literature, politics, anthropology or linguistics coverage. UCR has no African-language acquisition, Africa-based study, area-studies core or Africa-specific independent research course. The available adjacent courses cannot support an academically honest 24-course African Studies closest match.
